cases.description: Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a positive integer (2). Expected result is 10 / 2 = 5.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a negative integer (-2). Expected result is 10 / -2 = -5.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a non‑integer Number (2.5). Expected result is 10 / 2.5 = 4.
Attempt to divide by zero. The underlying Num implementation throws an ArithmeticException; the test verifies that the exception propagates.
Pass a null Number. The method should throw a NullPointerException before delegating to the overloaded method.
Divide a zero constant indicator (value 0) by a positive integer (2). Expected result is 0 / 2 = 0.
Divide a zero constant indicator (value 0) by a negative integer (-2). Expected result is 0 / -2 = 0.
Divide a negative constant indicator (value -10) by a positive integer (2). Expected result is -10 / 2 = -5.
Divide a negative constant indicator (value -10) by a negative integer (-2). Expected result is -10 / -2 = 5.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a negative fractional number (-2.5). Expected result is 10 / -2.5 = -4.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a very small positive number (0.0001). Expected result is 10 / 0.0001 = 100000.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a large integer (1000). Expected result is 10 / 1000 = 0.01.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a Float instance representing 2.0. Expected result is 10 / 2.0 = 5.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a BigDecimal created from the string "2". Expected result is 10 / 2 = 5.
Divide a positive constant indicator (value 10) by a negative fractional number (-0.5). Expected result is 10 / -0.5 = -20.
Pass NaN as a Double. The Num implementation should reject non‑finite numbers and throw IllegalArgumentException.
Pass positive infinity as a Double. The method should detect the non‑finite value and throw IllegalArgumentException.
Pass negative infinity as a Double. The method should reject the value and throw IllegalArgumentException.
Pass NaN as a Float. The underlying Num conversion should fail and raise IllegalArgumentException.
Pass positive infinity as a Float. The method should throw IllegalArgumentException due to non‑finite input.
Pass negative infinity as a Float. The method should throw IllegalArgumentException because the number is not finite.
